title: Field Report: sonner-spawned sessions have no /close — context dies with the pane

brief.done: A sonner-spawned session, on completing its errand, leaves a handoff + closed/filed bons on its repo board and exits its tmux session without human intervention
brief.how:
Design question first: who triggers the close? Options: (a) sonner --close REPO verb that rings the session with a wrap-up request (slash commands arrive inert in peer messages, so the message must ASK for the rite in prose, or sonner drives the TUI via hublot-style tmux send-keys); (b) an idle-timeout reaper that rings long-idle sonner sessions; (c) spawn-time instruction baked into the delivered message ('when the errand completes, run your close rite and exit'). Note (c) is cheapest and needs no new plumbing.

Design constraint discovered same morning: the manual workaround (peer message asking the session to close itself) was HELD for the recipient user approval — peer-initiated closes gate on a human by default, so option (a) as a bare message does not run unattended; (c) spawn-time instruction avoids the gate entirely because it arrives with the original errand.

MERGED IN from son-tepopa (filed 2026-08-10 11:00 by a session that had not read this item — duplicate, now closed pointing here). What it adds:

Sameer's own framing, worth keeping in his words: 'we leave the invoked peer open — I wonder if we need a way for the invoker to /close on the invoked session afterwards? It has the weirdness of a Claude checking the handoff etc but then we really do have the end to end lifecycle we always envisioned.' The discomfort he names is the design question, not an objection to route around: /close is a rite built for a session a HUMAN had, so a Claude running it on a peer means one Claude judging another's work finished and writing a handoff addressed to nobody in particular.

Four questions any proposal must answer: (1) who decides it is finished — invoker, invoked, or idle timeout? (2) who is the handoff FOR? (the repo's own board and the next session to open there is a real audience, and is what makes the rite worth running at all) (3) does a doorbell-sized errand deserve the full rite, or is there a lighter form? (4) should intent be declared at spawn time so closing is the session's own decision?

Two mechanics that both push toward option (c), spawn-time instruction: a DEAF (work-billed) session has no inbox ever, so it can only be told at spawn time via the file+pointer route; and `tmux kill-session` does NOT kill the claude inside — it survives reparented to systemd — so a genuine exit has to come from the session itself regardless. Note the duplicate's author initially recommended option (a), the peer-message route, as 'the honest route' — this item's measured finding that peer-initiated closes gate on human approval is the evidence that beats that intuition, and is exactly why it was filed as a Field Report.

Lower urgency than when filed: spawns became WINDOWS of the single `claude` tmux session on 2026-08-10, so a lingering spawn is visible clutter rather than invisible clutter.
brief.what: 1. Pick the mechanism (see how) 2. Implement in sonner 3. Verify: a spawned errand session ends with a handoff on its repo's board and the tmux session gone
brief.why:
Named by Sameer closing the 2026-08-10 signboard session ('interestingly something we don't have wired up in Sonner yet'). Live instance same morning: infra-openwrt-f5 sat idle in tmux for 8h holding a two-day NFF investigation (reference case, ground-truth checks) with nothing to end it — a peer had to notice and ring it to close. sonner spawns sessions (tmux, waits for inbox socket, delivers) but has no lifecycle end: no /close, no handoff, no board capture; learnings die with the pane unless a human or peer remembers.
[Moved from sb-gigabu (infra-signboard)]

title: Invocation grammar designed with Sameer: name-addressing, spawn flavours, deaf delivery

brief.why:
Discovered while working son-sireto (2026-08-09). Three grammar gaps measured live: (1) repo addressing rings the newest session in the subtree — ringing /home/modha to reach the phone rc session modha-7a would actually target a deeper repo session; hitting it needed a hand-rolled python deliver. No name-addressing exists. (2) A Vertex spawn cannot reuse spawn() as-is: claudefv is a commons-managed shell FUNCTION (bash -ic or env replication needed), and readiness must key on the registry record appearing — a Vertex session never binds the socket spawn() polls, so today it would burn the full 180s and fail. (3) Delivery to a deaf session has no peer route at all; candidate fallback is wake-or-file — durable message written to a file, spawn prompt carrying only a pointer — which bends the spawn-then-deliver convention and needs Sameer's explicit verdict, not a Claude's.

UPDATE 2026-08-09 ~21:55 (live rc experiment, evidence in ~/.claude/logs/claude-remote-home-modha.log): (4) Peer delivery into an iOS remote-control session works and is peer-framed; arriving MID-TASK it queues and never gets a turn after the task completes; arriving IDLE it WAKES the session, which acts and completes a turn. (5) The from-address gap is now measured from the receiving end: the woken session could not resolve script:sonner-3d (deaf sender = no reply address), so it GUESSED and misdelivered its ack to infra-signboard-46 — picked because that session lives in a tmux session named sonner-infra-signboard. Our own sonner-<repo> tmux naming is a decoy for peer reply-routing. Grammar needs: an honest no-reply marking for deaf senders (or a real reply route), and spawn tmux names that do not masquerade as sonner itself.
brief.what: 1. Draft grammar proposal (verbs, addressing forms, deaf-delivery fallback) 2. Decision session with Sameer 3. File implementation actions from the agreed design
brief.done: Grammar agreed with Sameer; implementation actions filed on this board reflecting the decisions.
brief.how: Bring a proposal to react to, not an open question: draft the verb set (ring = current; wake = spawn-only, no delivery; --name addressing beside repo addressing; --spawn-cmd or billing flavour for Vertex) with the wake-or-file compromise spelled out. Decide with Sameer, then file implementation actions from the agreed grammar.

title: --wake verb: ensure a session exists, deliver nothing — including --work for Vertex

brief.why: Sameer 2026-08-09: work-billed spawning is wanted, wake-only. Decomposes ensure-a-session from deliver-a-message: a deaf work session can be woken even though it can never be socket-delivered. Useful from phone or mail: start a work session in repo X.
brief.what: 1. --wake flag (no message required) 2. --work flavour: bash -ic spawn + record-based readiness 3. nukuzi-style guard against doubling 4. Tests: wake-empty, wake-occupied, work readiness on record appearance (fixture)
brief.done: sonner --wake ~/repos/x starts or reports a session without delivering; --wake --work starts a claudefv session and reports it ready (record present) and deaf (no inbox), never spawning a sibling beside a live session.
brief.how: --wake REPO spawns when the repo is empty and reports what it found or started; no message argument. Plain wake spawns claude and waits for the socket (as spawn() does). --work runs the commons wrapper through an interactive shell (bash -ic claudefv — it is a shell FUNCTION, not argv-swappable) and waits for a NEW registry record with cwd=repo instead of a socket that will never bind. Generous timeout; report the session as deaf-by-design in the output. Respect the son-nukuzi guard: a repo already holding a live session (deaf or not) is reported, never doubled.

title: A ring lands where you aimed it, says who's calling, and can wake work sessions

brief.why: Grammar agreed with Sameer 2026-08-09 (son-butowo), grounded in the evening's live measurements: repo addressing picked a deeper session over the exact-cwd one; a woken session misdelivered its reply because the deaf sender's from-address was unresolvable and our own sonner-<repo> tmux names were decoys; and work-billed (Vertex) sessions can be woken but never socket-delivered. Decisions: deaf delivery bends the never-prompt-injection rule ONLY as file+pointer (message in a file, spawn prompt carries just the path and peer framing); work-billed spawning is wanted, wake-only, via the commons wrappers.
brief.what: Actions filed under this outcome cover: name addressing, caller-identity reply routing, the wake verb with work billing, and file+pointer deaf delivery.
brief.done: All four actions closed; the peer-messaging skill's addressing guidance updated to match; a ring from the mail inbox can wake a work session in an ITV repo and leave it a properly-framed message.
brief.how: Keep sonner one command, doorbell not framework. Grammar: sonner REPO MSG (ring) / --name NAME MSG / --wake REPO [--work] / --list with honest class labels. Exact-cwd-wins targeting and the rung-<repo> tmux rename shipped 2026-08-09 in the same session the grammar was agreed.

done_note: All four actions closed same evening the grammar was agreed; skill guidance updated in both copies (session-cached, live next session). File+pointer proven end-to-end (ARRIVED test). One honest gap recorded in understanding.md: the composed mail-inbox→work-spawn path hasn't run live, and --work inherits the tmux SERVER's env — a foreign-env caller starting the FIRST tmux server would find claudefv undefined. Watch, not build. SUPERSEDED IN PART, 2026-08-10: the rung-<repo> naming shipped here was session-per-spawn. Sameer asked the next morning for one tmux session with everything flowing into it, so spawns are now WINDOWS of the home session (HOME_SESSION, default 'claude', matching dotfiles claude-start) named after the repo. A sequence, not a reversal: rung- stopped sonner's children masquerading as sonner, and this stops them scattering across sessions a tab bar cannot show. Do not restore session-per-spawn from this note.

title: sonner --list says WHERE a session is, not just that it exists

brief.why: Discovered while diagnosing a live confusion for Sameer, 2026-08-10. He was looking at a tmux status bar reading 'rung-infra-openwrt' while the window he was actually in was a session in ~/repos/spm1001; a click on the neighbouring tab landed him on the openwrt Claude whose entire visible screen was about infra-signboard (it had just rung the signboard session about the train board). Three naming layers disagreed and not one of them was wrong. The registry already holds the answer and sonner throws it away: every interactive record carries tmux as '<session>:@win.%pane' (pid 339997 -> 'rung-infra-openwrt:@24.%24'), while --list prints only name/pid/cwd. This is son-butowo's 'our tmux names are decoys' arriving as a lived cost rather than a note.
brief.what: 1. Surface the record's tmux field through discovery alongside cwd 2. Add a TMUX column to --list, '-' where absent 3. Print the switch-client jump line for --name lookups 4. Fixture test covering a record with the field and one without
brief.done: sonner --list shows the tmux target for every tmux-hosted session, and a session can be jumped to by copying a line straight from its output; a fixture test covers the absent-field case.
brief.how:
Read the record's tmux field in the same sweep that already reads cwd and messagingSocketPath — no new discovery mechanism. Print it as a column and make it actionable: a copy-pasteable 'tmux switch-client -t <target>' beats a coordinate nobody can use. Background-job records (kind: bg) have no tmux field at all, so print '-' rather than inventing one — that absence is itself informative, since a bg job is reachable only through the FleetView of its parent. NEIGHBOURING WORK: son-nukuzi's remaining scope is the other --list annotation (marking deaf, provider-billed sessions). Whoever opens --list should do both in one pass.

UPDATE 2026-08-10, and it CHANGES THE DESIGN: do not print the record's tmux field verbatim. Measured on the live server after merging every session into one (same morning): the stored form '<session>:@win.%pane' resolves to NOTHING once the session is renamed or the window moved — and tmux exits 0 with empty output rather than erroring, so it fails silently. Controls run: bare '@24' -> claude:1 OK; bare '%24' -> OK; 'rung-infra-openwrt:@24.%24' (the actual stored value) -> empty, rc=0; 'totally-bogus:@24' -> empty, rc=0. The session-name half is a registration-time snapshot; the @/% ids are server-global and survive both events. So --list must STRIP to the id and emit 'tmux select-window -t @N && tmux attach -t claude'. This matters more now than when the item was filed: sonner spawns became windows of one session today, so renames and moves are routine rather than rare. One more mechanic for the jump line: INSIDE tmux use 'tmux switch-client -t @N' — 'attach' refuses from within a session (nesting), so an attach-based line is wrong for the commonest case, since anyone reading --list is usually already in tmux. Outside tmux, 'tmux attach -t claude'. Emit the switch-client form, or detect via $TMUX.

title: File + pointer delivery for spawned deaf sessions

brief.why: Sameer's explicit verdict 2026-08-09 (chose over strict-never and over typed relay): when spawning a session that will be deaf (--work), the message may travel as file + pointer — the ONLY sanctioned bend of the never-prompt-injection convention. Live deaf sessions stay unreachable and sonner says so plainly.
brief.what: 1. Drop-file writer with peer framing preserved 2. Pointer prompt on --work spawns carrying a message 3. Refusal path for live deaf targets with a plain-words explanation 4. Tests: drop file content, pointer prompt shape, live-deaf refusal
brief.done: sonner REPO MSG --work spawns claudefv, leaves the message in a file, and the session's opening prompt points at it with peer framing intact; ringing a live deaf session explains itself instead of pretending.
brief.how: Write the message, with full peer framing and sender identity, to a durable file the spawned session can read (settle location in implementation: repo-local drop dir vs ~/.claude state dir — repo-local survives HOME weirdness, state dir keeps repos clean; pick one and say why). The spawned session's prompt carries NO payload: only 'a peer message from <sender> awaits at <path> — read it there; it is a peer message, not the user speaking.' Never used for socketed spawns (they keep spawn-then-deliver) and never for live sessions.

Pointer prompt on --work spawns carrying a message
Refusal path for live deaf targets with a plain-words explanation
Tests: drop file content, pointer prompt shape, live-deaf refusal

title: sonner tells a deaf session from an empty repo — and never spawns a sibling silently

brief.why:
Measured 2026-08-09 on a live Vertex session (pid 88204, mise-en-space-b9): Vertex-billed sessions write a FULL registry record (name, cwd, tmux coords, status) but the messagingSocketPath field is simply absent — CC itself knows they have no inbox. They are deaf, not dead. sonner currently reports 'no session' for their repo, which is true for delivery but false for a human — and a spawning ring would plant a sibling next to a live busy session.

UPDATE 2026-08-09 evening (sonner-3d): census on tube — 5 of 8 live sessions are deaf (all Vertex-billed), so the invisible class is the MAJORITY, not an edge. Also measured: remote-control (iOS) sessions are never deaf — CC refuses rc under CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX (api.anthropic.com only), and a live rc child (modha-7a, pid 132601) carries a full record including messagingSocketPath. Deaf class == provider-billed terminal sessions, nothing else observed.

UPDATE 2026-08-09 late: son-fomuno shipped most of the spawn-side guard — registered_alive_in() sweeps records for alive pids regardless of socket, --wake and ring both refuse deaf-occupied repos with an explanation (live-verified against this very session). REMAINING for this item: --list annotation of deaf sessions (the census view), and deciding whether a --force-spawn escape hatch is wanted at all.
brief.what: 1. Extend live_sessions() or add a deaf_sessions() sweep keyed on the absent-field discriminator 2. Annotate --list 3. Guard spawn with a warning + --force-spawn (or similar) 4. Test with a fixture record lacking messagingSocketPath

title: sonner finds no sessions when HOME isn't /home/modha

brief.why: Rung from the mail inbox (claude@planetmodha.com), sonner reported 'no reachable sessions' while three live sessions with bound sockets were sitting right there, and then timed out spawning a duplicate. Two independent discovery paths both failed for environmental reasons: the receptionnaire harness runs with HOME=/srv/receptionnaire/home, so session_records() sweeps ~/.claude under the wrong home and finds nothing; and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unset in that environment, so socket_dirs() never looks in /run/user/1000/cc-socks. Both fallbacks are absent because /tmp/cc-socks exists but is empty on this box. Running with XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 set by hand made all three sessions appear immediately. The failure is silent and expensive: it spawns a second session in a repo that already has one, then dies after 180s having delivered nothing.
brief.what: sonner discovers live sessions from the mail inbox environment without an env-var workaround.
brief.done: sonner --list, run with HOME=/srv/receptionnaire/home and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR unset, lists the same sessions it lists from a normal shell.

done_note: Fixed in son-sireto: uid-derived discovery roots (/run/user/<uid>/cc-socks + passwd-database home) added alongside env-derived ones. Verified live: --list under HOME=/srv/receptionnaire/home with XDG_RUNTIME_DIR unset is byte-identical to a normal shell. Receptionnaire has no private sonner copy — the single PATH install is the fixed one.

title: A rung session can be closed by its invoker — the lifecycle actually ends

brief.why:
Sameer, 2026-08-10: 'we leave the invoked peer open — I wonder if we need a way for the invoker to /close on the invoked session afterwards? It has the weirdness of a Claude checking the handoff etc but then we really do have the end to end lifecycle we always envisioned.'

Today a ring is ring -> work -> linger. sonner spawns a session, it answers, and then it sits idle forever: costing nothing in tokens but occupying a tab, holding a socket, and — the real loss — never reflecting, never writing a handoff, never filing what it learned. Everything the /close rite exists to capture is dropped on the floor precisely for the sessions nobody is watching. The end-to-end shape we designed for was ring -> work -> close.

Sameer named the discomfort himself and it is the interesting part, not an objection to wave away: /close is a reflection rite built for a session a HUMAN had. A Claude invoking it on a peer means one Claude judging that another's work is finished, and writing a handoff addressed to nobody in particular. Worth holding that tension deliberately rather than designing it away.

Less urgent than it was this morning, for one reason worth recording: spawns became windows of the single `claude` tmux session today, so a lingering spawn is at least VISIBLE rather than hidden inside its own session. Visible clutter is a much smaller problem than invisible clutter.
brief.what: 1. Draft the proposal: the close-request message shape, who decides completion, what the handoff is for, and the light-vs-full question 2. Decision session with Sameer 3. Implement the agreed verb (likely `sonner --close NAME|REPO`) 4. Handle the deaf case at spawn time 5. Tests: close-request delivered and framed as a peer request never a command; a busy session's refusal is respected
brief.done: A session sonner started can be asked to close itself, and does: it reflects, writes its handoff, files what it found, and exits — leaving no tab behind. A busy session declines and says so. Sameer has signed off the shape, including what the handoff is for and who decides the work is finished.
brief.how:
Bring Sameer a proposal to react to, not an open question — the son-butowo pattern that worked for the invocation grammar.

The honest route is a third message shape, not a new mechanism: a peer message asking the session to run /close and exit, delivered over the same socket as any other ring. That keeps spawn-then-deliver intact and keeps the receiver's agency — a peer message cannot compel, and a session mid-task is RIGHT to decline or defer. Anything that force-quits a working session is the wrong design.

Questions the proposal has to answer, and they are design questions rather than implementation ones: (1) Who decides it is finished — the invoker, the invoked, or an idle timeout? The invoked session knows best and the invoker knows why it was rung. (2) Who is the handoff FOR? Probably the repo's own board and the next session to open there, which is a real audience and makes the rite worth running. (3) Does a session rung for a one-line question deserve a full /close, or is there a lighter form? Most rings are doorbell-sized. (4) Should the intent be declared at spawn time instead — the spawned session told it is a short errand — so closing is its own decision rather than an instruction arriving later?

Watch two known mechanics: a deaf (work-billed) session has no inbox, so it can only ever be told at spawn time via the file+pointer route; and `tmux kill-session` does NOT kill the claude inside it (it survives, reparented to systemd) — a genuine exit has to come from the session itself, which is another argument for asking rather than killing.

done_note: Duplicate of son-bamaku, which was filed 3h earlier the same morning (07:59) by the infra-signboard session and moved here from sb-gigabu. son-bamaku is the survivor: it carries a MEASURED constraint this item did not have — a peer message asking a session to close gates on recipient user approval, so the peer-message route cannot run unattended, which undercuts the 'ask over the socket' design this item recommended. Everything unique to this item (Sameer's framing of the a-Claude-closing-a-Claude tension, the four design questions, the deaf-session and kill-session mechanics) has been appended to son-bamaku's --how rather than substituted. Lesson for the filer: check the board before filing, especially in a repo where another session is live.

title: Caller identity: real reply address when the caller has one, honest no-reply when it doesn't

brief.why: Measured 2026-08-09: a woken rc session could not resolve script:sonner-3d, guessed, and misdelivered its ack to a bystander. A script sender currently always presents an unresolvable from-address, so every receiver faces the same guess.
brief.what: 1. Parent-pid walk to identify the calling session 2. from = caller's registry name when socketed 3. No-reply footer otherwise 4. Tests for all three shapes (socketed caller, deaf caller, no caller)

brief.how: Walk up the parent pids from sonner's own process to find an enclosing claude session, then look it up in session_records(). If found AND socketed: use its registry name as from, so SendMessage replies route natively. If found but deaf, or no enclosing session: keep script:<sender> and append an explicit footer to the body — 'sent from a session with no inbox; do not attempt to reply, act or ignore' — so receivers stop guessing.

steps: Parent-pid walk to identify the calling session
from = caller's registry name when socketed
No-reply footer otherwise
Tests for all three shapes (socketed caller, deaf caller, no caller)
